  RECOMMENDATIONS FROM  PROPOSED POLICY REGARDING PUBLIC BENEFIT
  OFFICERS AND  PAYMENTS RELATED TO DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENTS
  DEPARTMENTS  WITH TAX-EXEMPT INSTITUTIONS
  Recommendation:
  (1) Find that the actions proposed in the agenda report are
  exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to CEQA State Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3)
  (Common Sense Exemption); and

  Council Minutes  11  07/15/2019
   (2) Adopt a policy whereby Development Agreements between
  tax-exempt institutions and the City of Pasadena include a Public
  Benefit Payment made by the institution.

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments and David
  Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  provided a PowerPoint presentation on the item and, jointly
  responded to questions.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the staff
  recommendation, stating that staff was asked to return to the City
  Council with a policy providing the specific details, standards and
  criteria related to the Payments in. Lieu of Taxes (PILOT). He
  expressed concerns with the controversial unintended
  consequences related to PILOT's, and the impacts this will have
  on non-profit organizations in the City, citing the ArtCenter College
  of Design (ArtCenter) as an example. He noted the problematic
  nature of imposing "taxes" on non-profit organizations, when
  legally they are tax exempt. Councilmember Madison spoke in
  opposition to the staff recommendation; and asked staff to provide
  information on the number of municipalities in California that utilize
  similar "PILOT' programs.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, which is designed to collect PILOT when a
  Master Plan and Development Agreement are proposed by a non-
  profit institution, which she believes is reasonable if such a
  proposed project will have an intensification of use at the site,
  which will result in an impact on City resources.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concerns that the Public
  Benefit Payment included with the ArtCenter's Development
  Agreement, noting that it appears to penalize the ArtCenter for
  providing dormitories, or affordable units, in the City; and spoke
  on the need for clear policy for the proposed PILOT program.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke on the need to provide clarity with
  the proposed PILOT program,.specifically on how staff will apply
  this to Master Plans and Develop Agreements moving · forward .
  He spoke on the inequity that such intensifications of use has on
  City residents by straining existing levels of service. He also
  spoke in favor of the staff recommendation, including a PILOT as
  part of a Master Plan and Development Agreement. He asked
  staff to provide detailed policy guidelines to ensure clarity on what
  data is used to determine the PILOT fees, and the policy must
  include a case by case review, as well as a comparative analysis
  on the benefits and additional burdens proposed by the Master

Council Minutes  12  07/15/2019
   Plan and Development Agreement, with staff to return to the City
  Council with an update.

  The Mayor spoke in support of the staff recommendation , and
  reassured the public that the staff recommendation is not a tax on
  non-profits, but rather a defined benefit to the City to cover
  increased service costs, in return for a significant benefit to a non-
  profit institution.

  Ken Hargreaves, External Relations Officer with California
  Institute of Technology (Caltech), expressed concerns with
  the staff recommendation.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember McAustin,
  seconded by Councilmember Gordo, to approve the staff
  recommendation , amended to direct staff to return to the City
  Council by September 2019 with a specific policy and guidelines
  applicable to any future public benefit payments to be collected for
  Master Plans and Development Agreements proposed by tax-
  exempt institutions:
